A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Rethinking Reward Model Evaluation: Are We Barking Up the Wrong Tree? All 22 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices 8.1–8.10, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original reward-model training and BoN/PPO experiments, accuracy–policy-regret correlations, and supplementary model, data, and KL-penalty analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and results, including Tables 1–4 and 7 and the appendix evaluations involving model scaling and MT-Bench.

M1.justification: The synthetic reward-model construction, NDR metric, response-expansion strategy, and BoN/PPO procedures remain unchanged in Sections 2–5.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same eight-source training mixture in Appendix 8.1, RewardBench categories and prompt-perturbation scenarios, and MT-Bench evaluation in Appendix 8.4.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same metric comparators, including Accuracy-pair, Bo5, ECE, and ξ correlation. Table 2 also retains the same response-source models and original RewardBench comparison.

E3.justification: Data splits, the 2,733-prompt evaluation, model configurations, metrics, annotation-budget controls, and optimization settings are unchanged. Appendix 8.10 still specifies N = 1,280 for the main BoN experiment.

E4.justification: The response-rank, prompt-perturbation, sample-size, annotation-budget, and overoptimization analyses are retained. Appendices 8.3–8.7 contain the same model/data variation, KL-penalty, and downstream-model checks.

E5.justification: Appendix 8.10 retains 64 test-dataset samplings, mean/variance reporting for Tables 2–4, and 95% confidence intervals for Figures 5–7. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their numerical results and trends. Table 1's Spearman correlations remain 0.7533 for BoN and 0.6102 for PPO; Figure 13 still reports 0.635 with p = 0.001. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The policy-regret and NDR definitions, Gaussian Regressional Goodhart assumptions, metric formulas, and Appendix 8.9 derivation are unchanged. Equation relocation and spacing introduce no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: accuracy incompletely predicts downstream performance, evaluation construction matters, and accuracy alone can miss potential overoptimization.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of BoN/PPO differences, prompt mismatch, annotation-budget limitations, and possible non-regressional Goodhart effects. No substantive interpretation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendices 8.1, 8.2, and 8.10 retain identical preprocessing details, prompt templates, OpenRLHF implementation information, and Table 8 hyperparameters. Technical and resource-access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The publication-status header does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v4 makes small wording and paragraph edits near the introduction, adds corresponding-author markers and an acknowledgments/funding paragraph, and updates the header to ICLR 2025 publication status. The scientific narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Limited reflow and spacing changes relocate unchanged displays: Table 5 moves from page 15 to 16, Figure 11 from 16 to 17, and Figure 14 from 18 to 19. Figure content, captions, axes, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the scientific argument, empirical evidence, mathematical content, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The attribution, acknowledgment, wording, and layout updates provide modest editorial polish without a meaningful net change in the paper's overall quality.
